title: Effects of functional diversity on ecosystem services in cocoa agroforestry systems in Costa Rica
abstract: Cocoa agroforestry systems (AFS) provide multiple ecosystem services, which are influenced by features of the shade tree community. By strategically selecting and managing shade trees based on their functional traits, cocoa farmers can affect functional diversity of AFS and potentially enhance the benefits they deliver. In this research, we applied functional trait ecology to better understand the effect of functional diversity of cocoa AFS on three ecosystem services: carbon storage, soil fertility, and provisioning of cocoa and other products. To achieve this, we characterized 30 AFS across a gradient of ecological complexity and established relationships between functional diversityw indices and ecosystem services using ANOVA and multiple regression models. As a result, two contrasting ecological dynamics were observed: low-complexity AFS, dominated by resource-conservative traits (higher leaf dry matter content, higher stem specific density, and low leaf nitrogen concentration), were associated with lower carbon stocks and soil fertility, while high-complexity AFS, characterized by resource-acquisitive traits (low leaf dry matter content, low stem specific density, and high leaf nitrogen concentration), delivered greater ecosystem services. Through the multiple regression analysis, we found that AFS dominated by species with greater maximum potential height, greater leaf nitrogen concentration, lower leaf dry matter content, lower leaf mass per area, and lower leaf nitrogen-phosphorus ratio were associated with higher carbon storage (R2 = 0.84), soil fertility (R2 = 0.7 for soil nitrogen), and multiple ecosystem services (R2 = 0.78). Additionally, cocoa yields were negatively correlated with shade cover and the dominance of large-leaf shade trees, revealing a potential trade-off between maximizing yields and enhancing ecosystem services. Nevertheless, the models indicated that a win-win scenario can be achieved when shade trees are productive, generating additional benefits. Finally, our study highlights critical relationships between shade tree traits and delivery of key ecosystem services for farm sustainability and farmer livelihoods.
abstract_zh: 可可农林复合系统（AFS）提供多种生态系统服务，而这些服务受遮荫树群落特征的影响。可可种植者若能基于遮荫树的功能性状进行有策略的选择与管理，便可影响农林复合系统的功能多样性，并有可能增强其所提供的效益。在本研究中，我们运用功能性状生态学，以更好地理解可可农林复合系统的功能多样性对三类生态系统服务的影响：碳储存、土壤肥力，以及可可及其他产品的供给。为此，我们在一个生态复杂度梯度上对30个农林复合系统进行了表征，并使用方差分析（ANOVA）和多元回归模型，建立了功能多样性指数与生态系统服务之间的关系。结果显示出两种截然不同的生态动态：低复杂度的农林复合系统以资源保守型性状为主（叶片干物质含量较高、茎比重较高、叶片氮浓度较低），其碳储量和土壤肥力较低；而高复杂度的农林复合系统以资源获取型性状为主（叶片干物质含量较低、茎比重较低、叶片氮浓度较高），能够提供更多的生态系统服务。通过多元回归分析，我们发现，以最大潜在高度较高、叶片氮浓度较高、叶片干物质含量较低、单位面积叶质量较低以及叶片氮磷比较低的物种为主的农林复合系统，与更高的碳储存（R2 = 0.84）、土壤肥力（土壤氮，R2 = 0.7）以及多种生态系统服务（R2 = 0.78）相关联。此外，可可产量与遮荫覆盖度以及大叶遮荫树的优势度呈负相关，揭示了在最大化产量与增强生态系统服务之间存在潜在的权衡。尽管如此，模型表明，当遮荫树具有生产力并能带来额外收益时，可以实现双赢的情景。最后，我们的研究凸显了遮荫树性状与关键生态系统服务供给之间的重要关系，这对农场的可持续性和农户生计具有重要意义。
